predecessors.name: Văn Lang
predecessors.text: Văn Lang, 'ruled by the Lạc Việt', whose 'lands were described as tidelands'

predecessors.name: Nam Cuong
predecessors.text: Nam Cương, 'ruled by the Âu Việt', who 'lived south of the Zuo River, in the You River basin, and in the upper Lô, Gâm, and Cầu river areas'

successors.name: Nanyue
successors.text: all of Âu Lạc, 'annexed' in 179 BC and 'divided ... into the Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen Commanderies'

ledger.x: 257 BCE: Thục Phán conquers Văn Lang and founds Âu Lạc at Cổ Loa.
179 BCE: Zhao Tuo annexes Âu Lạc.

wars.name: Nanyue conquest of Âu Lạc (179 BC)
wars.outcome: 'in 179 BC Zhao Tuo marched southward and successfully annexed Âu Lạc'; the land became the Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen commanderies of Nanyue.

certainty.note: A protohistoric kingdom known from Chinese and later Vietnamese texts; the shape is Cliopatria's throughout and the hill frontier toward the Zuo and You rivers is approximate.
